official.description: The NL Scholarship (formerly known as Holland Scholarship) is meant for international students from outside the European Economic Area who want to do their bachelor's or master's in the Netherlands. It amounts to EUR 5,000, received in the first year of studies, and is not a full-tuition scholarship.

verification.notes: Official Study in NL (Nuffic) NL Scholarship page read in full on 2026-10-10; confirms EUR 5,000 in the first year, the non-EEA nationality criterion, the no-Dutch-degree criterion, the not-a-full-tuition wording, the 1 November 2025 opening for 2026-2027 and institution-specific deadlines.

applicant_utility.summary: This is the national version of the NL Scholarship: EUR 5,000 once, in your first year, awarded by the institution rather than centrally, so your institution's own page is the only place the deadline and eligible programmes exist. It is explicitly not a full-tuition scholarship, so it should function as one line in a larger funding plan rather than the plan itself. The participating-institution list changes every academic year, so verify your programme's participation for the current round before relying on the money.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Non-EEA students entering a full-time Dutch bachelor's or master's at a participating institution who can fund the remainder themselves.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your institution and programme take part in the NL Scholarship for the current academic year
Open the institution's scholarship page and record its own deadline and document list
Check you hold no degree from a Dutch institution before investing time in the application
Prepare the institution-specific documents, which commonly include a motivation letter and a financial plan
common_rejection_risks: Applying to a programme the institution has not included in its NL Scholarship round
Waiting for a national deadline that does not exist and missing the institution's own closing date
Holding a prior Dutch degree, which is an outright eligibility bar
Treating EUR 5,000 as tuition coverage; the official wording says it is not a full-tuition scholarship
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition, living costs, insurance and travel are all uncovered; the award is a single first-year payment.
document_audit: Document requirements are set per institution; never assume the list you saw for another university applies
Where a financial plan is requested, it typically must cover the full programme duration
The award was renamed from Holland Scholarship to NL Scholarship, so archived guidance under the old name may be stale
alerts: Applications for an academic year open on 1 November of the preceding calendar year, so the 2027-2028 round opens around 1 November 2026
Nuffic's Integrity Code of Conduct excludes applicants involved in bankruptcy, tax or social-security default, money laundering, terrorist financing or related conduct
Admission and scholarship selection are separate processes at the institution; an offer of a place does not imply the award
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Pick a participating institution and programme, apply for admission through its own system, indicate or apply for the NL Scholarship as that institution instructs, upload its required documents, and await the institution's decision.

official.deadline_note: The application will be open from 1 December 2026 until 1 February 2027 (deadline: 31 January 23:59); applications received or incomplete after the deadline will not be considered.
official.status_note: The 2026-2027 round has closed; the page publishes the 2027-2028 round opening on 1 December 2026.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The tuition fee will be waived, both for students paying the statutory fee or the institutional fee; for non-EEA/EU students EUR 2,695 is waived through the scholarship and the residual EUR 18,305 is paid by the school.
benefits: Tuition fee waived (statutory or institutional); for non-EEA students the school pays the residual above the statutory amount
Living allowance equal to EUR 1,200 per month, so EUR 14,400 for one academic year
Personal allowance equal to EUR 249 granted once
Immigration fee (if applicable) equal to EUR 228 waived
eligibility: Full-time first-year master students with excellent results, both from EEA and non-EEA countries
Must have never been enrolled before as a full-degree master student at an educational institution in the Netherlands (a pre-master programme at ESE followed by an ESE master is allowed)
Must be admitted to the Master in Accounting, Auditing and Control, Econometrics and Management Science, or Economics and Business
Must have registered for one of these programmes in Studielink and submitted the application documents in the EUR Application Portal before 1 February 2027
Excellent previous results: average final result of at least grade 7.50 on a grading scale of 1-10
Must demonstrate via a detailed financial statement why the scholarship would enlarge the opportunity to study at ESE
Must eventually be enrolled no later than 1 September of the academic year; only students with an admission offer will be considered
Must have completed the immigration application; students with a scholarship application are instructed to send it by May at the latest
requirements: Motivation letter: motivation to study at ESE, evidence of being an excellent student and why the scholarship would expand the opportunity to study at ESE (max two A4, Arial, size 11)
Financial statement describing the financial situation and the reason and need for the scholarship (max one A4, Arial, size 11)
Budget plan using the EUR 'Budget plan' template
Certified copy of the most recent academic transcript with a wet stamp and signature of a school official; screenshots of online portals are not accepted
Certified statement from the educational institution confirming the obtained GPA (the ESE GPA template or an equivalent home-university statement)
documents: Budget plan on the provided template
Certified academic transcript with wet stamp and signature
Certified GPA statement from the educational institution
selection_criteria: Applications are reviewed after 1 February 2027 and all applicants are officially informed by email by 13 March 2027
Only one type of scholarship will be awarded to one applicant; applying for multiple is allowed but combinations are not awarded
The number of applications each year exceeds the number of available scholarships, so no rights derive from meeting the minimum criteria
coverage: Tuition fee waived (statutory or institutional; for non-EEA students the school pays the EUR 18,305 residual)
Living allowance of EUR 1,200 per month (EUR 14,400 per academic year)
Personal allowance of EUR 249 granted once
Immigration fee of EUR 228 waived where applicable
application_method: Register for an eligible ESE master programme in Studielink and submit the application documents in the EUR Application Portal before 1 February 2027
Gather the motivation letter, financial statement, budget plan, certified transcript and certified GPA statement
Submit the application online via Osiris student when the round opens on 1 December 2026
official.application_route: Apply online via Osiris student during the 1 December 2026 - 31 January 2027 window after registering for an eligible ESE master programme
official.citizenship_residency: Open to both EEA and non-EEA students, but never previously enrolled as a full-degree master student at a Dutch institution
official.international_eligibility: Open to students from both EEA and non-EEA countries
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Admission to one of three ESE programmes: Master Accounting, Auditing and Control; Master Econometrics and Management Science; Master Economics and Business
official.description: The Erasmus Trustfonds Scholarship at Erasmus School of Economics is designed for full-time first-year master students with excellent results from both EEA and non-EEA countries, amounting to a maximum of EUR 17,500 for the year 2027-2028.
official.program_type: University scholarship administered by Erasmus School of Economics

verification.notes: Official Erasmus School of Economics Erasmus Trustfonds page read in full on 2026-10-10; confirms the maximum of EUR 17,500 for 2027-2028, the tuition waiver mechanics including the non-EEA residual paid by the school, the EUR 1,200 monthly living allowance and EUR 249 personal allowance, the 1 December 2026 - 31 January 2027 application window, the three eligible programmes, the 7.50 grade requirement, the required documents, and the 13 March 2027 notification date.

applicant_utility.summary: At ESE the Trustfonds is a genuinely substantial package: tuition is fully waived (the school even pays the non-EEA residual above the statutory fee), you receive EUR 1,200 a month living allowance, a EUR 249 personal allowance and the EUR 228 immigration fee is waived. Only three programmes qualify, so if you are not admitted to Accounting/Auditing/Control, Econometrics and Management Science, or Economics and Business, this award simply does not apply to you. The documents are unusually strict: the transcript needs a wet stamp and signature, and portal screenshots are explicitly rejected, so request certified copies the moment your call opens.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Excellent first-year master's applicants (average 7.5+) to one of the three eligible ESE programmes who have never done a full Dutch master's degree and can document real financial need.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you are admitted or admissible to one of the three listed ESE programmes before preparing anything else
Request a certified transcript with wet stamp and signature early; screenshots are not accepted
Request a certified GPA statement from your university, matching the information in the ESE GPA template
Draft the financial statement to one A4 in Arial 11 explaining your situation and the reason and need for the scholarship
Budget using only the provided EUR budget-plan template
If you need a visa, send the immigration application by May at the latest rather than waiting for the 10 July deadline
common_rejection_risks: Any prior enrolment as a full-degree master student at a Dutch institution (an ESE pre-master followed by an ESE master is allowed)
A bachelor average below 7.50 on a 1-10 scale
Uploading an uncertified transcript or a portal screenshot instead of a stamped, signed copy
Switching programmes after being awarded: the scholarship only applies to the programme applied for
Assuming multiple ESE scholarships can be combined; only one type is awarded per applicant
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The package covers tuition and most living costs for one academic year; travel to the Netherlands and personal extras beyond the allowance are not covered, and the award applies to one academic year only.
document_audit: The motivation letter is capped at two A4 in Arial size 11 and must address motivation, excellence and why ESE specifically
The financial statement is a separate one-A4 document, not a paragraph inside the motivation letter
Only the provided budget-plan template is accepted
Certified means a wet stamp and signature from a school official; digital portal printouts are explicitly not accepted
alerts: The amount-and-payment section was scheduled to be updated in the third week of November 2026, so re-check the figures close to the application window
Applications open 1 December 2026 and close 31 January 2027 23:59; incomplete or late files are not considered
Current ESE master students cannot apply; the award is for incoming first-year students only
Enrolment must be completed no later than 1 September of the award year, and only applicants with an admission offer are considered
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register for an eligible ESE master in Studielink and complete the EUR Application Portal file before 1 February 2027, then submit the scholarship application in Osiris student between 1 December 2026 and 31 January 2027, and await the outcome email by 13 March 2027.
